project.name: rag-agent
project.description: RAG over hierarchical-header tables: one cell = one sentence, hybrid BM25+dense index, fine-tuned bge encoder, local Qwen reader.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel that re-exports the unified benchmark schema (BenchTable, BenchQuery, GoldOperand, Chunk) used by every dataset adapter under rag_agent.bench.

nodes.name: hitab.py
nodes.summary: Adapts raw HiTab tables and QA samples into the unified BenchTable/BenchQuery schema, resolving each query's gold data cells via hitab_grid's exact raw-to-data mapping instead of the old heuristic offset search.

nodes.name: hitab_grid.py
nodes.summary: Core HiTab addressing module: deterministically maps HiTab's raw text grid to its parsed data matrix by walking both header trees together, and resolves each query's gold cells (or header-carrier scope) from answer_formulas/reference_cells_map/linked_cells, replacing three previous heuristic joins that silently dropped large fractions of the population.
nodes.languageNotes: Tree-walking coordinate-mapping algorithm with monotone text-based child pairing to handle merged header cells; the module docstring documents the exact defect rates of the heuristics it replaces.

nodes.name: schema.py
nodes.summary: Defines the unified table/query/operand dataclasses (BenchTable, BenchQuery, GoldOperand, Chunk) that every benchmark loader normalizes into, so downstream retrieval/eval code is dataset-agnostic.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel re-exporting the HiTab sample/table loading functions from loader.py.

nodes.name: loader.py
nodes.summary: Low-level HiTab dataset I/O: locates the data root, loads JSONL QA samples and per-table JSON files from disk, and provides small accessors plus a debug pretty-printer for sample structure.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel re-exporting the core answer/retrieval scoring functions and difficulty classifier from metrics.py.

nodes.name: _bench_table_from_original
nodes.summary: Converts a parsed OriginalTable into a BenchTable by materializing its column/row header paths.

nodes.name: _operand
nodes.summary: Builds a GoldOperand for one data cell, normalizing its value to a float when possible and tagging it number vs string.

nodes.name: load_tables
nodes.summary: Loads and converts a set of HiTab tables (by id) into BenchTable objects for retrieval indexing.

nodes.name: load_queries
nodes.summary: Loads a HiTab split's QA samples and tables, resolving each query's gold operands via hitab_grid; every question is returned, with unresolved gold recorded as an explicit exclusion_reason rather than silently dropped.

nodes.name: norm_value
nodes.summary: Normalizes a cell value for comparison: numeric values by float value, text by lowercase/whitespace fold.

nodes.name: load_table
nodes.summary: Loads a HiTab table's raw and hmt (parsed) JSON pair from disk and builds the dual-addressable HitabTable.

nodes.name: axis_map
nodes.summary: Walks the raw and parsed header trees together to build a {raw line -> data line} map for one axis, pairing mismatched children by header text so a merged header cell can't shift its siblings.

nodes.name: formula_refs
nodes.summary: Parses a query's answer_formulas Excel-style cell/range references into raw-grid coordinates, reporting an unreadable_formula error when a formula's operator/reference can't be resolved.

nodes.name: gold_cells
nodes.summary: Resolves one query's gold answer cells to (table_id, row, col) triples via formula_refs (falling back to quantity_link), excluding queries whose gold lands on a header cell or an empty cell rather than silently truncating the gold set.

nodes.name: header_scope
nodes.summary: Finds every data cell governed by a header cell at a raw coordinate, used for queries whose HiTab-annotated answer is a header itself (e.g. "which region") rather than a value cell.

nodes.name: gold_target
nodes.summary: Returns the retrieval target for a query as either mode="all" (every resolved data cell must be retrieved) or mode="any" (one cell within a header's scope suffices), with an exclusion_reason when neither resolves.

nodes.name: answer_gold
nodes.summary: Resolves Strict Recall's gold set for a query from linked_cells' [ANSWER] coordinates (preferred) or answer_formulas as fallback, reporting an anomaly when the two sources disagree, and returning header-cell carriers separately from data cells.

nodes.name: HitabTable
nodes.summary: One HiTab table addressable in both raw-grid and data-matrix coordinate systems; builds row/col line maps on construction and fills any gaps left by merged header cells.

nodes.name: GoldOperand
nodes.summary: One answer-bearing data cell, identified by (row, col), its full header path, and a parsed numeric value when available.

nodes.name: BenchTable
nodes.summary: Unified table representation with per-row/per-column header paths and cell/path accessors, used by every benchmark adapter regardless of source dataset.

nodes.name: BenchQuery
nodes.summary: A natural-language question with its gold table, gold operands, and an explicit exclusion_reason when no gold could be resolved.

nodes.name: Chunk
nodes.summary: A serialized retrieval unit (chunk text plus the row/col cells it covers), used to check whether a retrieved chunk covers a gold operand.

nodes.name: _find_data_root
nodes.summary: Locates the HiTab data root by probing common subdirectory layouts (data/, HiTab/data/, or the given path itself).

nodes.name: load_samples
nodes.summary: Loads a HiTab split's QA samples from its JSONL file, optionally capped to max_samples.

nodes.name: load_table
nodes.summary: Loads a single HiTab table's JSON by id, probing both hmt/raw subdirectory depths the dataset ships with.

nodes.name: load_hitab
nodes.summary: Loads a HiTab split's samples and attaches each sample's table JSON, caching tables already loaded for a repeated table_id.

nodes.name: get_table_from_sample
nodes.summary: Returns the table dict attached to a sample, or the sample itself if none is attached.

nodes.name: get_query_from_sample
nodes.summary: Extracts a sample's natural-language question from whichever of question/sub_sentence/query keys is present.

nodes.name: get_table_id
nodes.summary: Resolves a sample's table id from its table_id field, its attached table, or its own id as a last resort.

nodes.name: get_answer
nodes.summary: Returns a sample's gold answer list.

nodes.name: print_sample_structure
nodes.summary: Debug helper that recursively prints a sample's shape (dict keys, list lengths, scalar values) to a bounded depth.

nodes.name: answer_em.py
nodes.summary: Classifies each HiTab query as lookup or arithmetic and scores predictions with the official (no-tolerance) EM plus a diagnostic format_defect flag for numerically-correct-but-differently-formatted answers; includes a self_check that verifies gold answers score EM=1.0 against themselves.
nodes.languageNotes: Korean-language module docstring documents a 2026-09-09 correction removing a lenient numeric_match-based metric after auditing showed it passed many false positives.

nodes.name: metrics.py
nodes.summary: Paper-aligned evaluation metrics: HiTab's own official answer scorer ported verbatim (for cross-paper comparability), a more forgiving internal numeric_match diagnostic, retrieval metrics (Recall@k, MRR, nDCG@k), and difficulty-class stratification mirroring the HiTab paper's appendix tags.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel re-exporting OriginalTable, TableIndex, and the OriginalStore back-compat alias from original_store.py.

nodes.name: original_store.py
nodes.summary: Ingest-time parser that turns raw HiTab table JSON into a 2D data matrix plus header-path trees (OriginalTable), with header-path lookup and Excel-ref helpers used by the symbolic-compute path; TableIndex is the in-memory map of parsed tables, not a retrieval store.

nodes.name: test_currency_scoring.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests verifying that a currency mark ($) is stripped symmetrically on both sides of hitab_exact_match_text without changing HiTab's own scores, and that RealHitBench-style comma-separated multi-value string answers are compared value-by-value.

nodes.name: test_hitab_grid.py
nodes.summary: Regression test asserting that hitab_grid's raw-to-data mapping covers every row/column of every test-split table and that gold resolves (and matches HiTab's published answer) for over 97% of queries, guarding against a silent shrinkage of the scoreable population.

nodes.name: test_strict_recall.py
nodes.summary: Test suite for the Strict Recall scoring scheme (whole-set, no-k coordinate scoring): covers exact/partial/empty prediction cases, threshold selection by macro-F1 with split isolation, header-carrier gold resolution, and MultiHiertt-specific gold spanning and evidence-anomaly detection.

nodes.name: query_type
nodes.summary: Classifies a query as lookup or arithmetic from HiTab's aggregation field.

nodes.name: em_official
nodes.summary: Scores a prediction against gold using HiTab's official free-text exact-match scorer, with no added leniency.

nodes.name: format_defect
nodes.summary: Flags predictions that the official scorer rejects but whose numeric values exactly match gold's, count for count -- a diagnostic for format-only errors, not an accuracy metric.

nodes.name: score
nodes.summary: Scores one query, returning its type plus official and format_defect flags.

nodes.name: self_check
nodes.summary: Verifies that scoring gold as its own prediction yields EM=1.0 per query type, surfacing failing examples so a normalization bug in one type doesn't hide in an aggregate score.

nodes.name: _to_nums
nodes.summary: Extracts every numeric value from a scalar, list, or string (currency/comma-aware) into a flat float list.

nodes.name: numeric_match
nodes.summary: Internal, deliberately forgiving numeric/substring match (+/-2% tolerance, x100/div100/abs variants) used only for diagnostic error analysis, not comparable to published HiTab accuracies.

nodes.name: exact_match
nodes.summary: Plain case-insensitive string equality against any gold value in a list, as a cheap sanity check.

nodes.name: _wtq_normalize
nodes.summary: WikiTableQuestions-style string normalization (accent/quote/dash folding, trailing-annotation stripping) used by HiTab's own official scorer.

nodes.name: _hmt_str_to_float
nodes.summary: Parses a HiTab answer string to float, stripping parens/percent/comma/dollar sign (currency stripping added by this project so a type mismatch can't fail a correct dollar-formatted answer), falling back to WTQ string normalization.

nodes.name: _hmt_process
nodes.summary: Recursively coerces a prediction/gold value (bool/number/string/list) into the typed form HiTab's official comparator expects.

nodes.name: _hmt_equal
nodes.summary: Type-strict equality used by HiTab's official scorer: strings exact, floats within 1e-5, lists element-wise.

nodes.name: hitab_exact_match
nodes.summary: HiTab's own official scorer ported verbatim, for producing numbers directly comparable to other papers' reported HiTab accuracy; requires pred already shaped like gold.

nodes.name: hitab_exact_match_text
nodes.summary: hitab_exact_match adapted for free-text LLM answers: splits a single-line multi-value answer on its natural separators before comparing value by value, with no other leniency added.

nodes.name: _multi_string_match
nodes.summary: Compares two comma/semicolon-separated multi-value STRING answers (e.g. RealHitBench's format) value by value, since the list-shaped branch above only fires when gold is an actual list.

nodes.name: recall_at_k
nodes.summary: Returns 1 if the gold table id is within the top-k ranked ids, else 0.

nodes.name: mrr
nodes.summary: Reciprocal rank of the gold id in a ranked list, 0 if absent.

nodes.name: ndcg_at_k
nodes.summary: Binary-relevance nDCG@k for a single gold id.

nodes.name: difficulty_class
nodes.summary: Maps a HiTab sample's aggregation tags and formula operator count to one of the paper's appendix difficulty classes, for stratified reporting.

nodes.name: _parse_paths
nodes.summary: Walks a HiTab top_root/left_root header tree to produce ordered leaf header paths and a line_idx-to-path map, dropping the synthetic root sentinel.

nodes.name: _to_float
nodes.summary: Parses a cell value to float (comma-aware), returning None when it isn't numeric; shared by hitab_grid's norm_value.

nodes.name: build_original_table
nodes.summary: Builds an OriginalTable from raw HiTab table JSON: parses the header trees, materializes the data matrix, and aligns each row/col to its header path by line_idx (falling back to leaf order).

nodes.name: OriginalTable
nodes.summary: Parsed 2D HiTab table with header-path lookup (exact word-bounded and fuzzy fallback), a to_dataframe view, and Excel-ref-to-coordinate translation for the symbolic-compute path.

nodes.name: TableIndex
nodes.summary: In-memory id-to-OriginalTable map built at ingest time; OriginalStore is a kept back-compat alias for the same class.

nodes.name: TestCurrency
nodes.summary: Verifies a currency mark is stripped from both prediction and gold symmetrically, wrong numbers still fail, and pre-existing HiTab normalizations (percent, comma, string case) are unaffected.

nodes.name: TestMultiValueStringGold
nodes.summary: Verifies comma-separated multi-value string answers (RealHitBench format) are compared value-by-value: order matters, missing spaces don't, and single-value gold is untouched.

nodes.name: test_every_table_maps_and_gold_resolves
nodes.summary: Asserts every test-split table's rows are fully mapped raw-to-data and that gold resolves for over 97% of queries, with bare single-cell references agreeing with HiTab's published answer on at least 98% of checked cases.

nodes.name: test_threshold_selection_is_variable_length_and_never_calls_budget_select
nodes.summary: Verifies threshold_select returns a variable-length, score-ordered cell set above a relevance threshold and never falls back to budget_select.

nodes.name: test_threshold_is_applied_only_from_another_split
nodes.summary: Verifies a relevance threshold chosen on one split (dev) is loaded and applied on another (test) only when the scoring config matches, raising on split reuse or a config mismatch.

nodes.name: test_summary_puts_precision_and_size_next_to_strict_recall
nodes.summary: Verifies the per-run summary reports macro/micro precision-recall and predicted-cell-count percentiles alongside strict recall, and that write() refuses to overwrite an existing output file.

nodes.name: test_hitab_header_answer_gold_is_the_header_cell_its_cells_carry
nodes.summary: Verifies answer_gold resolves a header-only HiTab answer to the header cell itself, whose carrier data cells all render that header in their row/column path.

nodes.name: test_mh_gold_spans_tables_with_dataset_cell_ids
nodes.summary: Verifies MultiHiertt gold cells spanning multiple tables resolve to dataset-style cell ids and that table-level coverage metrics (strict_recall, recall) are computed correctly across tables.

nodes.name: test_mh_text_only_questions_are_excluded_hybrids_kept
nodes.summary: Verifies MultiHiertt population loading excludes text-only questions by default, keeps hybrid table+text questions, and correctly tags each question's kind and program_ops.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the reconstruct module: re-exports the public header-path reconstruction functions from header_grid.py as the module's stable API.

nodes.name: header_grid.py
nodes.summary: Reconstructs hierarchical header PATHS (per-row and per-column) from a raw, blank-after-first 2D table grid by forward-filling each blank from its nearest non-blank ancestor, plus heuristics to guess the header-row/header-column boundary. Core algorithm behind the project's header-path reconstruction of real (non-gold) tables.
nodes.languageNotes: Encodes a sequence of versioned rule refinements (v2, v3, v3.1, v3.2, v3.3) directly in docstrings and parameter flags (e.g. close_on_total, disambiguate), each documenting a prereg'd hypothesis and its measured dev-set effect, including at least one rule kept but wired off after being measured and rejected (band_qualifiers).

nodes.name: _TableHTMLParser
nodes.summary: HTMLParser subclass that collects <tr>/<td>/<th> cells with their rowspan/colspan, tolerant of malformed markup (a stray missing '>' after the last attribute) found in scraped HTML.

nodes.name: parse_html_table
nodes.summary: Parses an HTML table into a blank-after-first 2D grid, resolving rowspan/colspan into an occupancy grid where a spanning cell's text sits only at its origin.

nodes.name: parse_html_table_layout
nodes.summary: Like parse_html_table but also returns a 'cover' map recording which original <td> produced each grid position, enabling header rule v3's span-aware reconstruction.

nodes.name: _hierarchical_carry
nodes.summary: Shared span-tracking forward-fill used by both the column and row axes: carries each depth's last non-blank label forward but cuts deeper carries whenever a shallower depth starts a new label, preventing a span from bleeding into a sibling's region.

nodes.name: _narrow_col_paths
nodes.summary: Header rule v3.1 (S1n): narrows the carry to only the labels whose declared colspan/rowspan actually covers the position, replaying the v2 carry and cutting contradicted labels while falling back to v2 when a cut would delete a column's year.

nodes.name: reconstruct_col_paths
nodes.summary: Builds one header path per data column from the header-row band, optionally using the markup-aware 'cover' map (rule v3 S1) or the narrow v3.1 variant.

nodes.name: section_label
nodes.summary: Returns the label of a SECTION row (exactly one filled cell and no data) or empty string, since a section row is the row axis's only way to express a header level the stub block has no column for.

nodes.name: band_qualifiers
nodes.summary: Finds single-value rows inside the column-header band (e.g. a lone 'percent' row) as candidate outermost row-path qualifiers. Measured and rejected on HiTab dev (0 gains, 110 losses) and left deliberately wired off in reconstruct_row_paths as a documented failed hypothesis.

nodes.name: reconstruct_row_paths
nodes.summary: Builds one header path per data row, mirroring reconstruct_col_paths: prepends section-row levels as a nested stack, applies v3/v3.1/v3.2 refinements (span-aware blanking, total-row section closing, tied-path disambiguation) behind explicit flags.

nodes.name: _total_names
nodes.summary: Header rule v3.1 (S4n): true for a bare Total/Subtotal row, or one whose text carries every (stemmed, stop-word-stripped) word of the section heading it would close.

nodes.name: _split_identical_paths
nodes.summary: Header rule v3 (S5): disambiguates data rows that reconstructed to identical paths by appending the nearest section headings above them (not already on the path) until the tied group is told apart, guarded by v3.1/v3.2/v3.3 refinements (closed sections, dated headings, numeric headings).

nodes.name: parse_html_table_with_merges
nodes.summary: Like parse_html_table but also returns the merged_regions span geometry instead of discarding it, so span markup can be consumed directly rather than re-inferred from blanks.

nodes.name: _fill_merges
nodes.summary: Returns a rectangular copy of the grid with every merged region's origin text written into every cell it covers, using exact markup-given span geometry instead of heuristic inference.

nodes.name: reconstruct_paths_with_merges
nodes.summary: Markup-aware counterpart to reconstruct_col_paths/reconstruct_row_paths: exactly fills spans from merged_regions and lifts a full-width header-band qualifier row (e.g. 'percent' spanning every data column) onto the row axis instead of the column axis.

nodes.name: _label_row
nodes.summary: Header rule v3 (S3): true when a row has 2+ filled non-stub cells and none of them looks like data, widening the v2 bare-year rule to catch footnoted years, dates, and text-leaf label rows.

nodes.name: corner_scope
nodes.summary: Header rule v3 (S6): extracts the top-left corner block's text as a date scope for undated columns, only when it contains a four-digit year and no column/row path already carries one.

nodes.name: _section_boundary
nodes.summary: True when a row is a section row (per section_label) that is not a parenthesised units note, since a section row structurally ends the header block even though its stub is blank and it holds no numbers.

nodes.name: guess_n_header_rows
nodes.summary: Guesses how many top rows are column headers using a blank-corner signal (primary) and a numeric-ratio fallback, with rule variants v1/v2/v3 controlling which label-row heuristics gate the corner scan.

nodes.name: _col_unlabeled
nodes.summary: True when column c is blank across every header row, meaning a stub group label spans over it rather than it being a real data column.

nodes.name: guess_n_header_cols
nodes.summary: Guesses how many left columns are row headers using a blank-tail signal (primary) and a content-type scan (fallback), with extension/capping rules for group labels spanning unlabeled stub columns and index/code columns.

nodes.name: point3_reconstruction_cost.py
nodes.summary: Experiment script isolating how much of the project's retrieval gain from header-path cell serialization is real structure vs reconstruction noise, by comparing retrieval on HiTab's gold header tree vs the reconstructed tree vs a shuffled-ancestor control.

nodes.name: shuffle_ancestors
nodes.summary: Permutes each header path's ancestor prefix across lines while keeping its leaf label, the control that isolates whether a retrieval gain comes from real hierarchy structure or merely from longer strings.

nodes.name: build_table_paths
nodes.summary: Returns per-data-cell gold and reconstructed (row_path, col_path) pairs for one HiTab table by aligning the benchmark table onto the real raw grid and running the texts-only reconstructor at the gold header boundary.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: builds five serialization arms (flat, gold, reconstructed, shuffled-control, gold-truncated-control) over aligned HiTab tables, encodes them densely, and reports set-EM@k retrieval accuracy per arm to quantify the reconstruction-error cost.

nodes.name: tree_reconstruct_hitab_raw.py
nodes.summary: Evaluation script (tree-reconstruction experiment C): feeds HiTab's real source grid to the reconstruct_{col,row}_paths functions and scores the reconstructed header paths against HiTab's gold hmt tree, reporting exact-match, segment-F1, and parent-child edge P/R/F1.

nodes.name: tree_lines
nodes.summary: Walks a raw top_root/left_root header tree and returns the grid lines the tree assigns headers to plus the grid lines the header block itself occupies.

nodes.name: _align_axis
nodes.summary: Monotone matching of gold data lines onto candidate grid lines by leaf label, used when the raw tree's line count does not already match the benchmark's data-row/column count.

nodes.name: align
nodes.summary: Maps HiTab benchmark-table (hmt) data indices onto raw grid line numbers and verifies the mapping by cell-value equality, excluding a table rather than scoring it on a guessed correspondence when verification fails.

nodes.name: norm
nodes.summary: Normalizes a header path (strip, lowercase, drop empty segments) into a tuple for exact-match comparison; imported and reused by point3_reconstruction_cost.py.

nodes.name: segment_f1
nodes.summary: Graded multiset-F1 agreement between a gold and reconstructed header path, reported alongside exact match as a softer metric comparable to the table-structure-recognition literature (TEDS/GriTS).

nodes.name: hierarchy_edges
nodes.summary: Converts a set of header paths into parent->child label-pair edges (root edges included), the unit used by Chen & Cafarella's hierarchy extractor and TUTA, reported as a companion metric to exact path match.

nodes.name: score_table
nodes.summary: Scores one table's reconstructed header paths against gold: aligns the table, determines the header boundary (known or guessed), runs the configured reconstructor (texts-only, merge-aware, or an injectable row_fn), and computes exact-match, segment-F1, and hierarchy-edge P/R/F1.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: iterates HiTab tables, scores each with score_table under the requested boundary/merge/TreeThinker options, aggregates results by size bucket and header depth, and writes a JSON report.

nodes.name: test_header_col_boundary.py
nodes.summary: Tests guess_n_header_cols on real RealHiTBench table shapes where the row-header region has to reach past a numeric group-code or index column to the column that actually holds the row's name.

nodes.name: test_header_v3.py
nodes.summary: Tests for header rule v3 (PREREG-2026-09-14-header-v3.md) — restores the source table's own row/column correspondence via span-aware carry, total-row section closing, tied-path disambiguation, and dated-corner scope, each test pinning one conversion defect by shape while checking v2's output stays unchanged.

nodes.name: TestHeaderColBoundary
nodes.summary: unittest.TestCase covering guess_n_header_cols on real RealHiTBench table shapes where a numeric country-code or BLS indent-level column sits inside the row-header region, ensuring the stub extends far enough to reach the actual row-label column.

nodes.name: test_rows_without_markup_and_padded_cells_keep_the_v2_carry
nodes.summary: Pins that header rule v3's span-aware carry (S1) leaves the v2 inferred carry unchanged for rows/positions with no span markup.

nodes.name: test_a_total_row_closes_its_section
nodes.summary: Tests header rule v3's S4: rows after a Total/Subtotal row leave that row's innermost section stack.

nodes.name: test_closing_a_section_keeps_the_leading_scope
nodes.summary: Tests that S4's total-row section closing never removes the leading (table-wide) scope, only inner section levels.

nodes.name: test_identical_paths_are_split_by_the_nearest_heading_above_them
nodes.summary: Tests header rule v3's S5: data rows that reconstruct to identical paths get disambiguated by the nearest section headings above them not already on their path.

nodes.name: test_build_tables_v3_applies_the_rules_and_v2_is_unchanged
nodes.summary: Integration-style pin confirming v3's combined S1/S4/S5/S6 rules change the intended cases while the v2 (default) reconstruction path stays byte-for-byte the same.

nodes.name: test_header_v3_1.py
nodes.summary: Tests for header rule v3.1 (PREREG-2026-09-14-header-v3.md 정정 1) — v3 narrowed to the side effects it was measured to have: each test pins a v3 side effect by shape and checks v3.1 no longer does it while v3's behavior stays reproducible.

nodes.name: test_a_cut_that_would_delete_the_columns_year_falls_back_to_v2
nodes.summary: Tests that v3.1's narrowed column-path carry (S1n) falls back to the v2 carry when cutting a span would delete a column's four-digit year.

nodes.name: test_only_a_lone_blank_label_row_loses_the_inherited_label
nodes.summary: Tests v3.1's S2n guard: a run of blank-label rows is treated as one visual group rather than a list of separately-emptied totals; only an isolated blank row loses its inherited label.

nodes.name: test_a_total_closes_only_the_section_it_names
nodes.summary: Tests v3.1's S4n: a total row closes a section only when its text names that section's heading, not any open section.

nodes.name: test_bare_and_plural_totals_close
nodes.summary: Tests that S4n's heading-name match tolerates a bare 'Total'/'Subtotal' and plural/singular differences.

nodes.name: test_a_closed_heading_is_not_put_back
nodes.summary: Tests that once a total row closes a section, that heading does not reappear on later rows' paths.

nodes.name: test_a_heading_with_another_year_is_not_added
nodes.summary: Tests v3.1's S5n disambiguation guard: a candidate heading dated with a different year than the row's own path is refused, even if it would otherwise split a tied group.

nodes.name: test_build_tables_v3_1_keeps_the_case_fixes
nodes.summary: Integration-style pin confirming v3.1's combined S1n/S2n/S4n/S5n guards apply together without regressing the cases v3 already fixed.

nodes.name: test_header_v3_2.py
nodes.summary: Tests for header rule v3.2 (PREREG-2026-09-14-header-v3.md 정정 3) — v3.1 minus two error types a mechanical check found v3.1 introduced that v2 had not; each test also pins v3.1's own behavior for reproducibility.

nodes.name: test_a_named_sub_total_does_not_close_a_section_whose_own_total_is_still_below
nodes.summary: Tests v3.2's S4n2: while a section's own exact 'Total <heading>' row is still below, any other named total in between is treated as a sub-total that does not close the section.

nodes.name: test_a_bare_total_does_not_close_it_either
nodes.summary: Tests that S4n2's own-total guard also withholds section closing from a bare Total row when the section's own total is still below.

nodes.name: test_the_own_total_of_the_same_heading_further_down_does_not_count
nodes.summary: Tests the boundary of S4n2's own-total lookahead: a same-named total row appearing after (not below within scope of) the current section does not count as its own total.

nodes.name: test_a_number_is_not_a_heading_that_tells_rows_apart
nodes.summary: Tests v3.2's S5n2 disambiguation guard: a candidate heading that is itself a number is refused as a disambiguator for tied row paths.

nodes.name: test_build_tables_v3_2_is_v3_1_with_the_two_rules_replaced
nodes.summary: Integration-style pin confirming v3.2 equals v3.1 with only S4/S5 replaced by S4n2/S5n2, leaving v3.1's other guards (S1n, S2n, S4n) intact.

nodes.name: test_header_v3_3.py
nodes.summary: Tests for header rule v3.3 (PREREG-2026-09-14-header-v3.md 정정 4) — v3.2 with S5n2 replaced by S5n3: when refusing a numeric heading would make disambiguation reach past it for a higher heading, the tied group is left at its v2 path instead.

nodes.name: test_build_tables_v3_3_is_v3_2_with_s5n3

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: This is a master's thesis codebase studying RAG over hierarchical-header tables: how to index a table's data cells (with their row/column header paths and table title attached) so that a shared retriever can find the right cells and hand them to a shared reader. The README frames the comparison as an indexing-representation ablation — this project's own S3c cell-sentence scheme against row-preserving markdown chunking, a character-chunking baseline, and a RowCol HiTab adaptation — all measured on HiTab's 991-question single-cell test set with a BGE+BM25 hybrid retriever and a local Qwen reader held constant.

tour.title: Package & Dependencies
tour.description: rag_agent/__init__.py is the package root; its docstring documents the cell-per-sentence indexing scheme and hybrid BM25+dense retrieval design that Step 1's README describes, and it declares __version__. pyproject.toml is the Hatchling packaging config that pins the ML/retrieval stack (torch, transformers, faiss-cpu, rank-bm25, groq) the rest of the tour will use, and declares an optional 'benchmarks' extra for the MultiHiertt dataset covered later in the tour.
tour.languageLesson: pyproject.toml under a [tool.hatch] table is Hatchling's build backend config — TOML's [section] headers group settings, and dependency arrays pin exact versions so a research codebase's numbers stay reproducible across machines.

tour.title: Running an Experiment
tour.description: retrieval_accuracy.py is the codebase's highest-fan-out file (11 outgoing edges) — it builds the hybrid BM25+dense corpus across every serialization scheme (S1/S2/S3/S3c/TableRAG-units), runs budget- or threshold-based cell selection, and reports per-query pass/fail retrieval accuracy. answer_accuracy.py is its companion: it scores the reader's answer against exactly the context that retrieval actually delivered, not a re-derived approximation. With no single main.py, these two CLI scripts are the de facto entry points that wire every subsystem covered in the rest of the tour together.

tour.title: Cell Serialization: One Sentence Per Cell
tour.description: base.py defines the shared Chunk/TableView primitives every serialization scheme builds on. templates.py defines the STRUCTURAL template (this work's S3c index unit), plus the render() function that substitutes title/row-path/col-path/value into sentence text. caption.py is the serializer that actually walks a table and emits one such sentence per data cell. This is the project's central idea from Step 1 made concrete: a hierarchical header path flattened into indexable text.

tour.title: Alternative Serialization Baselines
tour.description: tablerag_unit.py ports Google TableRAG's cell/column index-unit scheme (categorical cell docs plus deduplicated numeric-column summaries) as a comparison baseline. chunks.py instead converts a table to markdown text and splits it into overlapping chunks by character count or tokenizer, reproducing the row-preserving markdown and character-chunking arms the README compares against S3c. Because Step 3's scripts swap these in under the identical retriever and reader, any accuracy difference can be attributed to representation alone.

tour.title: Hybrid Retrieval Index
tour.description: encoders.py is the single most depended-upon file in the graph (10 incoming edges): it defines the Encoder interface plus a hashing bag-of-words fallback and a SentenceTransformer/BGE dense encoder, including the E5/BGE-style query-prefix handling that fine-tuned dense retrieval needs. sparse_bm25.py reimplements BM25Okapi ranking with sparse CSR matrices so the ~468k-sentence HiTab corpus fits in ~200MB instead of several GB. hybrid_index.py fuses the two via min-max normalization or reciprocal rank fusion. Whatever cell sentences Steps 4-5 produced get embedded, scored, and ranked here — the shared retriever the README holds constant across every serialization arm.

tour.title: LLM Reader Backends
tour.description: base.py defines the abstract BaseLLM interface every backend implements, including a shared last_finish_reason attribute used to detect truncated outputs. factory.py parses a 'backend:model?query' spec string and constructs the matching implementation. local_qwen.py is the default backend — a self-contained local Hugging Face Qwen model with 4-bit/8-bit quantization baked into the run's identity, so a resumed run can never silently mix results across quantization levels. Once Step 6's retrieval returns evidence, this is the shared reader the README compares every serialization scheme under.
tour.languageLesson: BaseLLM is a Python abstract base class (ABC): it declares the methods every backend must implement without providing a default body, so factory.py can construct any concrete backend and call it through one interface without knowing which one it got.

tour.title: Scoring Retrieval and Answers
tour.description: metrics.py ports HiTab's own official answer scorer verbatim (for cross-paper comparability) alongside Recall@k/MRR/nDCG@k retrieval metrics and difficulty-class stratification. answer_em.py classifies each query as lookup or arithmetic and scores it, including a self_check that verifies gold answers score EM=1.0 against themselves — a sanity check against a broken scorer silently reporting zero. strict_recall.py implements the set-based Strict Recall scoring (no top-K re-cutting) used for the project's evidence-pack results. These are what Step 3's two scripts call to turn raw predictions into the numbers in the README's results table.

tour.title: Evidence Provenance & Integrity
tour.description: artifacts.py is the second most depended-upon file in the codebase (9 incoming edges): it hashes, JSONL-persists, and strictly schema-validates the evidence records shared across both the HiTab and MultiHiertt evaluation scripts. It exists so answer_accuracy.py (Step 3) can prove it scored the reader against exactly the context retrieval actually delivered, closing the loop between retrieval accuracy and answer accuracy instead of letting the two scripts silently drift out of sync.

tour.title: Reconstructing Hierarchical Headers
tour.description: header_grid.py is the core algorithm behind Step 4's S3c sentences on tables that don't ship pre-parsed headers: it forward-fills each blank cell in a raw table grid from its nearest non-blank ancestor to recover per-row and per-column header paths, plus heuristics to guess where the header region ends. treethinker.py is an alternative that reconstructs the same header-path shape via one cached LLM call per table (RealHiTBench's TreeThinker prompt) instead of the deterministic forward-fill algorithm, letting the project compare structural reconstruction against a model-based one.

tour.title: Loading HiTab Tables and Queries
tour.description: original_store.py is the ingest-time parser that turns raw HiTab table JSON into a 2D data matrix plus header-path trees. hitab.py adapts those parsed tables and QA samples into the unified BenchTable/BenchQuery schema (defined in schema.py), resolving each query's gold data cells via header_grid's exact raw-to-data mapping from Step 10 instead of a heuristic offset search. This is where the pipeline traced through Steps 3-10 actually begins: raw dataset files become the BenchTable objects that Step 4's serialization turns into cell sentences.

tour.title: Generalizing to MultiHiertt
tour.description: retrieval_accuracy_mh.py and mh_arms.py reuse Step 3's arm/unit-selection code against a MultiHiertt table adapter, adding multi-cell (m>=2) lookup and arithmetic query strata, so a 'retrieval arm' means the same thing on both datasets. answer_accuracy_mh.py mirrors answer_accuracy.py's incremental, crash-safe, resumable scoring for MultiHiertt. This is the project's second benchmark, run under the same shared retriever (Step 6) and reader (Step 7) design established earlier in the tour.

tour.title: Tests as Living Documentation
tour.description: test_hitab_grid.py is a regression guard asserting that Step 10's header_grid raw-to-data mapping covers every row/column of every test-split table and that gold answers resolve correctly for over 97% of queries — protecting against a silent shrinkage of the scoreable population. test_strict_recall.py exercises Step 8's Strict Recall scoring scheme across exact/partial/empty prediction cases, threshold selection, and MultiHiertt-specific edge cases. In a codebase with no single runtime entry point to smoke-test, these pytest files are where correctness claims actually get pinned down.
